pairs.question: Dicite, quae causa uiae? quisue ora repente peruasit pallor? cur scire futura libido?
pairs.derivation: Proteus the seer questions the sea-nymphs; speech tag 'ait' (429) stripped, and first-word capitalization kept from 'Dicite'. Cymodoce's reply answers his 'quae causa uiae / quis pallor' with the operative first sentence 'Nosti nostros, praesage, timores' (their fears are the cause); cut before the following lines 'quid Tyriae classes... habitabimus antra?' which turn from answering to posing her own counter-questions.
